#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR increases the timeout for liveness probe from 5s to 10s.
This test is mostly flaking on dockershim started failing more frequently from 18/11.  Tried searching but couldn't find any suspected PR. Ran locally as well with same environment(ubuntu+dockershim) but no flakes observed locally. 
Since this test is failing alot in kubeadm kinder jobs proposing to increase timeout for now.

that is a different test

This test has an interesting history https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/100036 , since previously an timeout on exec was considered ok, since the bug was clear but it changed the current behaviour, the fix was added behind a feature gate.

If someone wants to dig, first we should check if the feature gate for the exec probe timeout is set or unset

confirmed flakes

Since Liveness probe is timing out here, container is restarted and we are not getting expected timeout 
Also the feature gate is default enabled https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/features/kube_features.go#L553
The timeout for probe is 5 secs, maybe we should increase it to 10?

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-cluster-lifecycle-kubeadm#kubeadm-kinder-kubelet-1-21-on-latest

if the infra is getting a lot of pressure for a period of time (e.g. tests in these jobs are concurrent) increasing the timeout would make sense.

oddly these tests use 2 second ticks:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f572e4d5b4a1496356eccf29c34adac02280beeb/test/e2e/common/node/container_probe.go#L751
so odd numbers are not a good pick as the cap...
IMO 5 second seems low for a restart, also the tick should be 1 second.

but before increasing timeouts and adjusting ticks it is worth checking if something actually changed that slowed down restarts...

Liveness probes are timing out which is causing the container restarts.

Looking at the timing of the flakes, is it possible that we're seeing a performance regression on containerd because it does not yet support the v1 CRI? I'm not seeing any flakes of this test on CRI-O:

- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-cri-o#ci-crio-cgroupv1-node-e2e-conformance&include-filter-by-regex=%2Ftmp%2Fhealth&width=5
- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-cri-o#ci-crio-cgroupv2-node-e2e-conformance&include-filter-by-regex=%2Ftmp%2Fhealth&width=5

> Looking at the timing of the flakes, is it possible that we're seeing a performance regression on containerd because it does not yet support the v1 CRI? I'm not seeing any flakes of this test on CRI-O:

Is the fallback in kubelet expensive? Naively I wouldn't expect this to be an issue, and it seems like that would be problematic for folks upgrading?

We can move KIND (and other CI) up to a containerd 1.6 beta release with https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/5619/commits/a5c417ac060f29dad343573674f879d59fc0b9ef but it's not clear to me if we should be doing that or fixing missing v1 cost on the Kubernetes side

Shouldn't there be more flakes if containerd V1 CRI is the reason? Also this job runs on dockershim https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-informing#gce-ubuntu-master-default
